How Each Lesson Is Organized

Consistent four-part structure across primary and intermediate grades so students and teachers always know where to find source material and practice.

1. Pupil’s / Student’s Book

Page-referenced dialogues, reading texts, grammar tables, and step-by-step classroom activities faithful to the printed book.

Core study

2. Workbook

Interactive matching, sentence completion, grammar drills, and self-check answer guidance clearly separated from Student’s Book pages.

Guided practice

3. Vocabulary

Clean, structured word and phrase tables organized by topic, with accurate word-level Arabic meanings isolated cleanly for bilingual study.

Word reference

4. Lesson Test

Lesson Tests are independent assessments that measure each lesson’s learning objectives, vocabulary, and grammar using new questions and contexts without copying book exercises. Navigated one question at a time and scored instantly, published tests hold between 10 and 20 questions.

Independent check

For Teachers

A single entry point to the published lessons, the answer-key areas, and an honest list of the material that does not exist yet.

No sign-in

Teacher Portal

The teacher portal collects the twenty prepared lessons, the answer-key areas published on nineteen lesson tests, and the practice answer reveals that pupils can already open. It also states plainly what is not available: no audio key, no round test, no teacher’s guide, and no accounts or pupil records.

The classroom password on the answer-key areas only hides those answers from casual view. It is not authentication and does not protect confidential material.

This portal is a directory for teachers, not a separate system. Every link here opens a page that exists in this repository: twenty prepared Unit 1 lessons across Grades 3, 4, 5 and 8, their Pupil’s or Student’s Book, Workbook, Vocabulary and Lesson Test pages, and the answer-key areas that are published on nineteen of those tests.

Scope of this portal No sign-in

No accounts, no student records

Opening this portal creates no account and asks for no personal details. Nothing here records marks, attendance, completion or pupil progress, and there is no dashboard to maintain.

The only browser storage in the whole platform is the single “Continue learning” page link kept on this device by the student pages. The teacher pages never write to it, so opening them cannot disturb a pupil’s saved place.

How the answer-key areas work — and what they cannot do

Read this before showing a key in class. The honest description matters more than the convenience.

Display aid only

One shared classroom password hides the key; it does not protect it

Not secure authentication. The answer-key areas on nineteen lesson tests ask for a single classroom password typed into the page. It is not authentication: that password only hides the key from casual view, and the key text is already part of the published page, so anyone can read it in the browser without typing anything. Do not treat the password as a security control, and never place confidential information, unpublished material, marks or personal data behind it.

Genuine access control needs a server to check each request before the answers are sent. This site is a static publication with no server-side component, so that check does not exist here. Adding one is a later architectural step and is not part of this phase; until then the honest position is that the keys are public teaching material with a courtesy screen in front of them.

For the same reason, the practice answer reveals on the book and Workbook pages are open to everyone, including pupils. They are useful for self-checking and for projection, but they are not hidden material.

The classroom password is deliberately not printed anywhere on this portal. If you need it for your class, contact Eng. Somer Shaheen on WhatsApp.

Running a prepared lesson

The four sections keep their own page order, so a lesson can be taught in stops without mixing books.

01Open the lesson hub and choose the section you need; the shared section bar keeps all five pages one tap apart.
02Project the Pupil’s or Student’s Book page and read the printed activity aloud, exactly as it appears in the book.
03Move to the Workbook for guided practice. The on-page reveals can be opened in class when you want the answer shown.
04Set the Lesson Test, then open the answer-key area on the same page to review the items together.

What the published answers can and cannot tell you

Set expectations before marking: independent Lesson Tests assess lesson objectives with original items, while Book/Workbook reveals distinguish printed answers from inferences and mark missing audio openly.

Independent test items

Lesson Tests under the Independent Lesson Test Policy measure the lesson’s learning objectives, vocabulary, and grammar using new questions and contexts rather than copying book exercises.

Objective-aligned

Printed in the source

Answers labelled as explicit are readable directly in the supplied book pages. The Grade 3 Lesson 2 and Grade 4 Lesson 2 keys label each item this way or as inferred.

Direct reading

Follows from the source

Answers labelled as inferred follow from the printed grammar, sequence or meaning where the book prints no key. They are teaching judgements, not publisher answers.

Labelled inference

Not available at all

No listening or audio answer key exists anywhere in this repository because no official recording was supplied. Those items stay unscored and unanswered on purpose.

Read this before using a key

These are teaching answer keys, not the publisher’s official answer key. Independent Lesson Tests assess the lesson’s learning objectives, vocabulary, and grammar with new questions and contexts rather than copying book exercises, and their keys give the expected answer, target objective, and explanation. On Book/Workbook practice reveals and earlier source-referenced keys, answers printed in the book are distinguished from labelled inferences. No listening answer has been invented anywhere, because no official recording was ever supplied.

Answer-key areas sit inside nineteen lesson tests and are hidden behind one shared classroom password typed into the page. That password is a display convenience only: the key text is already part of the published page and can be read in the browser without it. It is not authentication, and it must not be used to protect confidential or unpublished material. Real access control requires a server-side check, which this static site does not have.

The in-page reveal counts below are the “show the answers” controls that already exist on some book and Workbook pages. They are visible to pupils too — they need no password. Use them for self-checking or projection, and do not describe them to a class as hidden material.
